subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for September 26, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Comparative efficacy and safety of hydrocortisone-based regime
sentences: Story 1 is about Comparative efficacy and safety of hydrocortisone-based regimens in septic shock: A network meta-analysis..
This is a systematic review / meta-analysis from Journal of critical care.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in adults with septic shock (PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL; inception-May 1, 2025; PROSPERO CRD420251015672), how should we interpret and hydrocortisone 200-299 mg/day combined with fludrocortisone 50 μg/day were associated with reduced 28-day mortality compared with placebo (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29-0.96; OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.96, respectively), with higher fludrocortisone doses showing?
A total of 21 trials involving 7908 patients were included.

Hydrocortisone ≥300 mg/day and hydrocortisone 200-299 mg/day combined with fludrocortisone 50 μg/day were associated with reduced 28-day mortality compared with placebo (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29-0.96; OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.96, respectively), with higher fludrocortisone doses showing numerically greater point estimates of benefit, though estimates were not statistically significant.
Higher hydrocortisone doses were associated with increased superinfection risk, while fludrocortisone appeared to attenuate this effect.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.

The bedside implication is this: Potentially practice-relevant because a patient-centered outcome is reported; check absolute risk difference, adverse events, and whether your ICU population matches the study.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of hydrocortisone-based regimens in septic shock: A network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating hydrocortisone and/or fludrocortisone in adults with septic shock (PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL; inception-May 1, 2025; PROSPERO CRD420251015672). A total of 21 trials involving 7908 patients were included. Hydrocortisone ≥300 mg/day and hydrocortisone 200-299 mg/day combined with fludrocortisone 50 μg/day were associated with reduced 28-day mortality compared with placebo (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.29-0.96; OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.96, respectively), with higher fludrocortisone doses showing numerically greater point estimates of benefit, though estimates were not statistically significant. The optimal corticosteroid regimen for septic shock, particularly the dosing and combination of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, remains uncertain due to inconsistent mortality findings across trials. Interventions were grouped into six regimens (including placebo), and outcomes were analyzed using a frequentist random-effects model; the primary outcome was 28-day mortality.

This study examined the association between plasma copper (Cu) concentrations, endothelial injury markers, inflammatory burden, illness severity, and 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis.
